summary: No thesis broke on the news today. The four buys (KR, MSCI, VTI, CARG) were all outside the 5-day earnings window as the Portfolio Manager stated, and the filings in inputs/news.json confirm the dates: KR 12-03, CARG 11-05, MSCI reported on 10-20 (8-K 2.02 and 10-Q; the 10-27 estimate is stale), VTI is an ETF. Per lesson L2 I checked each name's own estimate and filings rather than relying on the earlier note. The only mild contrary signal was Moody's (MCO, not held) drawing a few price-target trims after its 10-21 double miss, which does not affect any holding.

MSCI post-print PT raises continue (JPMorgan $710, Evercore $726, Wells Fargo $720, Morgan Stanley $671, RBC $655), with no negative 8-K follow-up. WMT headlines are product news (AI Agent Gateway, Affirm and Sam's Club BNPL deal), constructive and not material. Market and sleeve context to watch tomorrow: futures were lower on Middle East escalation (US ordering staff out of Saudi Arabia, Brent about $111), BTC slid from the failed $84,300 breakout to about $82k while spot ETF inflows stayed positive ($528M), and Apple's iPhone Duo launches 10-23 with the Oct 28 event and 10-29 or 11-02 earnings next (not held). Outside the book, SAM and VRSN are estimated to report today (10-22) with no results headline yet; WDFC reported 10-21 (EPS $1.06 missed $1.15, sales beat, FY27 guide roughly in line); SMG's 8-K 5.02 from 10-16 is still unread; DORM (10-26), EXLS and INCY and LOGI (10-27), and CALX, CVS and GRMN (10-28) are the next high-risk prints for any new buy. For news-memory: the KR cyber-incident flag came to nothing so far (never attributed to Kroger), and the two-day TPR price-target cut thread has no new cut today (Tapestry only announced its earnings call date, so the 11-05 estimate is consistent).
